test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is Virgin Vegetation?

options.text: Vegetation grown as a part of afforestation programme
A plant community that has evolved naturally without human assistance and has long been abandoned by humans
A plant community that has been cultivated with human assistance

solution:
The correct answer is __**A plant community that has evolved naturally without human assistance and has long been abandoned by humans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Virgin vegetation** refers to plant communities that have grown naturally without any direct or indirect human intervention.
 
• This type of vegetation develops through natural processes of succession and evolution over a long period of time.
 
• It is distinguished from other types of vegetation by the absence of human activities such as cultivation, deforestation, or any form of land use.
 
• Virgin vegetation often includes a diverse array of plant species, many of which may be endemic or specially adapted to the local environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Afforestation Programme**

 
 
• Afforestation is the process of planting trees, or sowing seeds, in a barren land devoid of any trees to create a forest.
 
• The goal is to create forests in areas where there were no trees previously, which can help combat climate change, improve air quality, and increase biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Human-Cultivated Vegetation**
 
 
• This refers to plants and trees that are deliberately grown and maintained by humans for various purposes such as agriculture, horticulture, or landscaping.
 
• Cultivated vegetation is typically managed through activities like irrigation, fertilization, and pruning.
 
 
 
• **Natural Succession**
 
 
• Ecological succession is the process by which the structure of a biological community evolves over time.
 
• Two main types of succession are primary (starting from a barren environment) and secondary (following disturbance in an area that previously had vegetation).
 
• Succession leads to a stable climax community that is in equilibrium with the environment.
 
 
 
• **Endemic Species**
 
 
• Endemic species are plants or animals that exist only in one geographic region.
 
• These species are particularly vulnerable to extinction due to their limited distribution.
